summary: T2 verified correct and complete against all 5 acceptance criteria. IcsImportService converts bounded ICS bytes into native event batches preserving standalone, all-day, timed, recurrence-exclusion, and detached-override semantics. All 3 T2 service tests pass (and all 9 tests in the file pass). Implementation matches the approved architecture and program design; no defects found.
follow_up: T3 (authenticated HTTP endpoint) is now the first dispatchable task; it was waiting on T2. The byte limit is already exercised at the HTTP layer by T3's test ics_import_http_requires_calendar_content_and_bounds_the_body (oversized body -> 413).
important_context: T2 scope: backend/src/ics_import.rs (committed f8c39b9), backend/src/lib.rs (exports 'pub mod ics_import'), and the 3 ics_import_service_* tests in backend/tests/ics_import.rs. backend/src/event.rs and the test file are uncommitted modifications; ics_import.rs itself is committed with no diff.
Constants: MAX_ICS_IMPORT_BYTES = 1 MiB (tested at HTTP layer by T3), MAX_ICS_IMPORT_EVENTS = 1000 (tested at service layer by T2).
Status normalization: absent/CONFIRMED->Confirmed, TENTATIVE->Tentative, CANCELLED->Cancelled, unknown->InvalidCalendar (rejected).
Error categories: InvalidCalendar (orphan/mismatched/duplicate/unknown-status/malformed/invalid-UTF8), LimitExceeded (over event or byte limit), NotFound, Database.
All semantic validation happens before persistence; the service delegates exactly once to EventService::create_batch, so failures leave all tables unchanged (asserted via assert_table_counts(0,0,0)).
Re-import creates a separate editable native copy (events count 3->6 after re-import), not an idempotent upsert.
